thread:
support-ana: FYI — ACME just opened an escalation: p95/p99 for /v1/embeddings (eu-west-1) jumped ~3x at 04:12 UTC. They saw timeouts and some 502s. I attached their request IDs and a small trace.

mara: ack. Can you paste one of the request IDs and a sample trace? We'll triage.

support-ana: request ids: req_01F8XQ..., req_01F8XR... Trace snippet: 'upstream_write_timeout while proxying to runtime'. Customer reports latency spike started right after our 04:00 host kernel rollout in eu-west-1.

samir: interesting — we rolled kernel 6.4.3 -> 6.5.0 to eu-west canaries at 03:50. Also pushed a GPU driver micro-update to the dedicated pool at 03:55. Could be interaction.

ops-joe: alert from infra: host iowait on gpu nodes in eu-west-1 spiked at 04:10. Quick check:

ops-joe: ```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device:         r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s  r_await w_await  aqu-sz  %util
nvme0n1        12.34  4.50  2048.00 1024.00    0.00   0.00    0.50   1.20     0.80  95.00
``` 

infra-luca: dmesg on one node shows repeated NVMe admin timeouts after the kernel update:

infra-luca: ```
[ 2321.123456] nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout, resetting controller
[ 2321.124000] nvme nvme0: failed to reset controller
```

mara: ok that's pointing at storage IO interference. That explains embeddings p99 since KV cache misses hit disk and slow down token generation.

jess: quick mitigation request: can we reroute eu-west production traffic to the backup capacity pool (older kernel/firmware) while we triage? Also open to throttling background jobs on the same hosts.

samir: yes — I'm switching routing policy for embeddings route to prefer dedicated-backup-pool for eu-west. Will also scale up prewarmed pods to soak load. ETA ~4m.

ops-joe: rolling routing now. Command: `./infractl route update --route embeddings --region eu-west-1 --preferred-pool dedicated-backup-pool --weight 100` -> done. Traffic shift at 04:18 UTC. Customer reports immediate p95 improvement to baseline.

mara: great. Next step: repro on a canary node. I'll schedule a repro run to hit cache miss path and reproduce the NVMe timeouts.

infra-luca: repro logs attached. When running synthetic embedding load with cold cache we see increased NVMe commands latency after kernel 6.5.0. Reverting kernel to 6.4.3 on a single node removes the timeouts.

samir: conclusion for now: regression introduced by kernel 6.5.x change interacting with our NVMe firmware driver combo. Plan: rollback the kernel rollout on eu-west canaries, pause further kernel pushes, and open vendor bug with OEM. I'll create a Jira.

jess: mitigation checklist:
- [x] rerouted production to backup pool
- [x] scale up prewarm capacity
- [x] paused kernel rollout in eu-west
- [ ] vendor bug + kernel bisect (samir)
- [ ] customer postmortem & timeline (support-ana)

support-ana: shared update with ACME: "We've routed your requests to a unaffected capacity pool and are investigating a kernel/storage regression. We'll follow up with a timeline within 2 hours." They acknowledged :thumbsup:.

eng-sre-bot: Incident created INC-2026-3314, severity P2. Assigned: samir, infra-luca, mara.

mara: adding note — possible long-term mitigations: change KV-cache placement to ensure hot shards stay in RAM, add IO cgroups for background tasks, increase NVMe queue limits on specific instances, and consider FIO-based prechecks before kernel rollouts.

samir: opening vendor ticket now and starting kernel bisect on private lab (trying 6.4.13 -> 6.5.0 range). I'll post early findings here.

support-ana: thanks team. I'll keep ACME updated and link INC-2026-3314. If anyone needs me to coordinate customer calls ping me.

jess: great response — leaving this thread open until rollback validated and vendor response. :white_check_mark:
